title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from pages 20–23: a 'figure' F is a family of closed pieces A of an ambient space, each with an 'interior' A°. The interiors are pairwise disjoint and cover the support |F|, so they define an equivalence relation R_F on |F|. The pieces satisfy a frontier-type axiom: for A, B in F, A ⊂ B iff A° ∩ B ≠ ∅. A figure is thus essentially a regular cell or stratified decomposition of |F|, ordered by its face poset. The proposition being proved (pp. 20–21) gives conditions under which every A in F has a unique B = φ(A) in G with A° ⊂ B°, and φ: F → G behaves well.

On this page Grothendieck first notes that he still has to justify b) ⇒ b'). Several crossed-out attempts follow. He then proves that, granted b'), φ is increasing (order-preserving for inclusion). Here b') says: for every A in F there is B in G with A° ⊂ B°; and A ∈ F, B ∈ G, A° ⊂ B imply A ⊂ B.

Proof that φ is increasing. Take A, A' in F with A' ⊂ A, and B = φ(A), B' = φ(A'), so A° ⊂ B° and A'° ⊂ B'°.
- By b'), A° ⊂ B gives A ⊂ B.
- Hence A'° ⊂ A' ⊂ A ⊂ B.
- So A'° ⊂ B'° ∩ B, which is non-empty.
- By the frontier axiom in G, B' ⊂ B. QED.

He then defines: under these conditions F is a refinement of G, written F ≪ G, and states that this is an order relation.

Proposition: for figures F and G the following are equivalent.
- a) F ≪ G and F is extremal among refinements of G, for the sub-figure order ≤ on figures. The page writes 'minimal'; the next page makes clear 'maximal' is meant.
- b) F ≪ G and |F| = |G|.

The next page proves this. If |F| ≠ |G|, adjoining a point {x} with x in |G| \ |F| gives a strictly larger refinement. It also proves a corollary that disjoint refinements can be united. In modern terms this is elementary combinatorics of refinements of cell decompositions or stratifications: refinement induces a monotone map of face posets, and maximal partial refinements are exactly those with full support.
errors: Proposition item a) says 'minimal' among refinements; the proof on p. 23 shows 'maximal' (for the sub-figure order) is intended.
The implication b) ⇒ b'), needed to finish the proposition of p. 20, is announced but not proved here. It is only addressed via the corollary of p. 21 and margin notes, so a gap remains on this page.
The claim that ≪ is an order relation is stated without proof. Antisymmetry needs the support equality plus the interior conditions; this is plausible but not checked.

The proof that φ is increasing implicitly uses that interiors A'° are non-empty and that B = φ(A) is unique (pairwise disjoint interiors in G). These are axioms of 'figure' assumed from earlier pages.

ideas.what: Figures as families of closed pieces with disjoint interiors and the frontier condition A ⊂ B ⇔ A° ∩ B ≠ ∅
ideas.modern_name: regular cell complex / stratification satisfying the frontier condition; face poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (CW complexes), Whitney/Thom (frontier condition for stratifications)
ideas.where_published: Loosely related to the 'tame topology' and stratified spaces in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not in this form

ideas.what: Refinement F ≪ G of figures and the induced increasing map φ: F → G (A ↦ the unique cell B with A° ⊂ B°)
ideas.modern_name: refinement / subdivision of cell complexes; induced monotone map of face posets (carrier map)

ideas.what: Maximal refinements of G within the sub-figure order are exactly those with |F| = |G|

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification inside Grothendieck's private 'algebra of figures' (combinatorics of cell decompositions and their refinements). It is mildly interesting as documentation of his 1986 foundational work on tame or combinatorial geometry, but contains no result beyond elementary face-poset combinatorics.
transcription_corrections: The stars in 'A' ⊂ A* ⇒ B' ⊂ B*' and 'A* ⊂ B*' appear to be marks highlighting the statement to prove (A' ⊂ A ⇒ B' ⊂ B), not part of the notation; likewise the last line should read 'donc B' ⊂ B, qed'.
The first line reads approximately 'Il nous faudrait justifier b) ⇒ b') pour terminer [?] la dém. de la prop.'.
The rotated left-margin note reads roughly 'NB F ≪ G ⟺ ∀A ∈ F ... A ⊂ ... de F un raffinement ...'; it is largely illegible and should be marked uncertain.

In Proposition a), 'prenant ceux de F' is likely 'parmi ceux dont F est sous-figure'. The phrase 'minimal ... dans l'ensemble ≤ (relation des figures)' should read approximately 'minimal [maximal] parmi les raffinements de G (relation ≤ des figures)'.
